title: Client Concierge — Model Roster, Quant Experiments & Prompt Slimming Log
content:
Purpose:
This is a working log for the Client Concierge engagement (Client XYZ). Focus: pick a small, maintainable model roster + quant profiles that meet the client latency SLO (<200ms p95 for short queries), target token-cost reduction (~3–4x vs baseline hosted 13B fp16), and acceptable fidelity (>=92% of baseline LLM on our task-focused quality eval).

Context / workload characteristics:
- Production workload: short conversational Q/A + structured extraction from support transcripts (~50–200 tokens responses typical). Heavy tail of short prompts (mean prompt tokens ~25).
- SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms for 1–2 concurrent requests per connection (expected client throughput modest initially).
- Privacy: customer prefers private deployment (VPC) but initial POC will run on Redwood dedicated pool.

High-level goals for POC (measurable):
1) Latency: p95 <= 200ms for canonical short prompts on selected model/quant combo.
2) Cost: reduce token cost by >=3x vs baseline 13B fp16 while maintaining quality.
3) Quality: task-specific accuracy (F1/exact match depending on task) drop <= 8% relative to baseline.
4) Operational: simple rollout path with one canary and a fallback to baseline on regressions.

Model roster (candidates considered) — roster curated for diversity of architecture and quant-friendliness:
- baseline-13b-fp16: Baseline client reference (13B fp16). Quality target anchor.
- mixtral-7b-instruct: Good instruction following, compact. Evaluated at q4_0 and q8_0.
- guanaco-7b-compat: Very fast on small sequences, tested q4_0.
- llama2-13b-chat (quantized): candidate for higher quality, tested q4_0 and q8_0 but higher latency.
- local-13b-4bit: q4_0 variant with aggressive quantization (best case for cost).
- small-cascade-tier: 3-stage cascade family (tiny->7b->13b) — considered for hybrid routing.

Quant profiles tested (naming consistent with runtime):
- q4_0 (4-bit symmetric, fast kernel)
- q8_0 (8-bit, better fidelity, slightly slower)
- fp16 (baseline)

Experiment matrix (text summary — full CSV attached separately in linked_artifacts):
For each (model,quant,batch,kv_cache_on) we measured p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, quality delta (task accuracy % vs baseline), and token cost estimate. Representative rows below (short prompts):
- mixtral-7b / q4_0 / batch1 / kv=true -> p50 35ms p95 78ms, 480 tps, quality -6.2%, est cost 0.28x baseline
- mixtral-7b / q8_0 / batch1 / kv=true -> p50 46ms p95 95ms, 380 tps, quality -2.5%, est cost 0.42x
- guanaco-7b / q4_0 / batch1 / kv=true -> p50 30ms p95 72ms, 530 tps, quality -9.8%, est cost 0.24x (risk: hallucination on structured extraction)
- llama2-13b / q4_0 / batch1 / kv=true -> p50 78ms p95 210ms, 220 tps, quality -3.0%, est cost 0.55x (p95 slightly over SLO for short queries)
- local-13b-4bit / q4_0 / batch1 / kv=true -> p50 65ms p95 180ms, 260 tps, quality -4.8%, est cost 0.40x
- cascade (tiny->7b->13b) adaptive routing -> p50 28ms p95 160ms, weighted quality -2.1%, est cost 0.34x

Key observations from runs:
- q4_0 provides the biggest cost wins and latency improvements on 7b-class models, but fidelity penalty varies by family. Mixtral family showed the best fidelity/latency compromise at q4_0 in our tasks.
- llama2-13b quantized gives higher quality but p95 often edges past the 200ms SLO on our Dedicated pool for short queries — tolerable with small-scale traffic but risky if client scales.
- Cascade routing gives predictable p50 improvements and keeps p95 in range; complexity of prompt routing and fallbacks increases testing overhead.
- KV cache warmup matters: when session-based reuse was simulated, p95 dropped by ~15–25ms for repeated conversation turns. For the POC, enable prefix/KV caching for authenticated sessions.

Prompt & pipeline tuning notes (practical heuristics we iterated on):
- Prompt slimming: remove non-essential preambles ("You are a helpful assistant...") for short Q/A; keep instruction as a single-line role token when possible. Example before->after: 
  BEFORE: "You are a helpful assistant. Provide a concise answer with bullet points when helpful."
  AFTER: "Answer concisely; use bullets only if >40 tokens."
  Impact: trimmed input tokens by ~6 tokens average -> small latency reduction and fewer kv-cache misses.
- Structured output constraint: prefer JSON-schema style responses (explicit keys). This reduces token generation variance and often shortens decode length. Example system instruction used in tests appended: "Return JSON {"answer":..., "sources":[...] } only."
- Token budget enforcement: explicitly set max_tokens for short answers (e.g., max_tokens=120) to avoid runaway output.
- Pre-answer decomposition for extraction tasks: split long multi-part prompts into two stage pipeline (1: identify relevant excerpt, 2: extract fields). Slightly higher overall cost but reduced hallucination and better quality for structured data.

Cache and batching strategy notes:
- Continuous batching hurts short-tail latency; set runtime so short queries skip large batch windows (latency-first policy).
- Enable KV prefix caching for sessions, TTL=10m. Eviction policy: LRU with priority for active sessions (discuss with infra).
- Micro-batching (2–4) gives effect of higher throughput without p95 regression for short queries; we used dynamic batch cap that increases only when queue depth > 3.

Regression signals observed during quantized runs:
- Named-entity truncation: q4_0 variants occasionally truncated long proper names in extraction tasks. Mitigation: adjust prompt to expand context window for names, or fallback to q8_0 for extraction-heavy requests.
- Numeric fidelity: some q4_0 configs produce slightly off-by-one values when asked to extract counts. Add short post-processing checks (validate numeric ranges) in pipeline.

Decision log (current recommendation):
- Primary POC variant: mixtral-7b / q4_0 with session KV caching + prompt slimming heuristics. Rationale: meets latency p95 comfortably, cost reduction ~3.5x, quality drop within target (~-6% but acceptable for client tolerance).
- Secondary (quality fallback): local-13b-4bit / q4_0 deployed behind canary; use adaptive routing on quality-sensitive endpoints (extraction) -> sends those to 13b when validation checks fail.
- No-go for immediate full-swap to llama2-13b quantized because p95 risk during initial traffic burst; keep for later phase if we provision more Dedicated capacity.

Operational rollout plan (POC):
1) Week 0–1: Deploy mixtral-7b q4_0 to dedicated test pool + run synthetic traffic harness from linked_artifacts. Owner: Diego.
2) Week 1–2: Run A/B with 10% live traffic routing (canary) comparing to baseline 13b fp16. Measure p50/p95, task accuracy, and token-cost delta. Owner: Priya.
3) Week 2–3: Enable adaptive cascade routing for extraction endpoints. Owner: Tom.
4) Week 3: Review & decision: proceed to Dedicated reserved capacity or expand to Private. Owner: Asha.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Are our eval sets sufficiently representative of client production prompts? Action: get larger anonymized sample from client (see JIRA-4212).
- Latency behavior under concurrent warm starts (spike testing needed).
- Compliance: ensure quantized binaries meet client's verifier for on-prem (if we move to Private).

Quick repro commands (local harness examples):
- Run single-shot perf test (example):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE' -d '{"model":"mixtral-7b-q4_0","input":"Summarize: <transcript>...","max_tokens":80}'
- Run batch harness: python perf_harness.py --model mixtral-7b-q4_0 --concurrency 4 --qps 50 (script in linked_artifacts)

Test-case snippets (short list for regression harness):
- Short Q: "How do I reset my password?" (expected: steps, <50 tokens)
- Entity-heavy: "Transaction 0xF3A1B... occurred at 2024-05-01, summarize parties involved" (checks for name completeness)
- Multi-turn extraction: multi-message transcript -> extract {customer_name, issue_type, urgency}

Notes to self:
- Slack thread: #se-client-xyz has client expectation docs; double-check wording on "concise answers" (they prefer full sentences sometimes).
- TODO: add per-token embedding usage measurement for reranking experiments (low priority).

Next steps (near term):
- Diego: launch dedicated pool experiments and attach raw logs to gdrive artifact (due 2024-06-14).
- Priya: prepare A/B dashboard (cost, latency, quality) and share with client (due 2024-06-18).
- Tom: prototype adaptive routing policy and failover config (due 2024-06-21).

End of working log (iteration 2024-06-10).
